title: Give Your First Paycheck Four Jobs
meta_description: Turn a first paycheck into a repeatable system for essential bills, a starter buffer, costly debt, benefits and one future goal.

module_headings.external_sources: Primary Payroll, Banking and Tax Guidance

sections.heading: Treat the First Paycheck as a Systems Test
paragraphs: A first paycheck feels like permission to celebrate, repay everyone and upgrade life at once. It is also the first real test of a new financial system. Before assigning every dollar, verify what arrived, when the next pay arrives and which obligations must survive between them.

The useful number is net pay, not annual salary divided by twelve. Taxes, benefit elections, retirement contributions and payroll timing determine spendable cash. An hourly worker must also account for actual hours, overtime rules, unpaid breaks and a pay period that may not include every day already worked.

Give the paycheck four jobs in order: operate until the next payday, build a small buffer, address the most expensive or dangerous obligation, and fund a future goal. Celebration can be included inside the operating plan instead of consuming whatever remains by accident.

Do not make permanent commitments from one deposit. The first check can be partial because employment began mid-period, benefits may start later, tips or commissions can vary, and deductions can change. Wait for several normal pay cycles before choosing rent, a vehicle or subscriptions based on assumed income.

The opening photograph shows a check above a laptop because the first task is receipt and verification. Paper check, direct deposit and payroll card are delivery methods; the pay statement explains how gross earnings became the amount available.

Write the next thirty days on one page: pay dates, required bills, transport, food, work costs, debt minimums and one planned reward. This is a cash-flow map, not a moral scorecard. It prevents an early purchase from taking money needed before the second payday.

If family expects a contribution, discuss a sustainable amount after required work and living costs. Gratitude does not require promising a percentage the job cannot support. Separate a one-time gift from a recurring household obligation.

Keep enough cash for employment itself: commuting, uniforms, equipment, meals, childcare, connectivity and professional fees. Losing the ability to reach work in week two would undermine every other paycheck goal.

Create a “first check pending” rule: money is not available until the deposit clears, the pay statement matches hours and no urgent correction is needed. A banking app’s pending credit or a paper check in hand is not the same as settled funds.
The first paycheck succeeds when it establishes a repeatable path from work to safe deposit, bills, reserves and goals. The amount matters; the operating habit matters longer.

sections.heading: Read Every Line of the Pay Statement
paragraphs: Begin with employer name, employee name, pay-period dates and pay date. Confirm the period includes the shifts expected. A first check often covers fewer days than the worker assumes because payroll closes before payday.

Compare pay rate, regular hours, overtime, tips, commission, shift differential, bonus and reimbursement with time records and the offer. Gross pay is earnings before deductions. Year-to-date figures accumulate from the beginning of the calendar year with that employer.

[[S1|The CFPB pay-stub guide]] explains gross wages, federal withholding, payroll taxes, other deductions and net pay. Use the actual statement to translate each line. A label that is unclear should be taken to payroll or human resources, not guessed from social media.

Payroll taxes and income-tax withholding are different. Social Security and Medicare deductions can appear separately from federal and state income tax. Benefit deductions may be pre-tax or after-tax depending on the arrangement and current rules.

Confirm voluntary deductions: health, dental, vision, retirement, transit, union dues, flexible accounts, life or disability coverage. Match each with an election made during onboarding. A deduction is not automatically wrong because take-home pay is smaller than expected.

Reimbursements should not be confused with wages. If the employer promised repayment for travel, equipment or training, confirm timing and treatment. Save receipts and policy approval rather than assuming the first check includes every amount owed.

Compare hours with a personal record. Keep schedules, clock records and written correction requests. Wage-statement requirements vary by jurisdiction and work arrangement; contact the appropriate labor agency or qualified adviser when pay remains incorrect.

Check the bank deposit against net pay. Split direct deposit can send portions to multiple accounts, so the checking deposit alone may appear short. Verify all destinations before reporting a missing payment.

Save pay statements securely. They support budgets, withholding checks, benefit questions, rental applications and disputes. Do not leave unredacted statements in shared devices or email them casually because they can contain identity and account information.
The pay-statement review passes when dates, rate, hours, earnings, deductions and deposits reconcile. Report an error promptly in writing and continue keeping a record until corrected.

sections.heading: Choose a Safe, Low-Fee Place for Pay
paragraphs: A paycheck needs a secure landing place before it needs an investment. Compare checking or savings accounts at insured institutions, payroll cards and paper-check options by fees, access, protections, minimum balance, ATM network and timing.

[[S2|The CFPB explains]] that employers offering a payroll card must provide at least one other payment option. Direct deposit to an account the worker chooses can reduce loss and check-cashing fees, but the account’s own overdraft and maintenance terms still matter.

Confirm deposit insurance through the FDIC for banks or NCUA for federally insured credit unions, within applicable rules and limits. A payment app balance is not automatically the same as an insured deposit account; read the product terms.

Ask about monthly fees, minimum balance, overdraft, returned items, out-of-network ATM use, paper statements, early closure and instant-transfer charges. A signup incentive can be erased quickly by routine fees.

Use an account in the worker’s own lawful control. Minors may need an appropriate custodial or joint arrangement depending on age, institution and jurisdiction. Understand who can withdraw or close the account before directing wages there.

Set a unique password, multifactor authentication and account alerts. Protect the email and phone used for recovery. Never give a login or verification code to someone claiming payroll must “confirm” the deposit.

If using a paper check or mobile deposit, endorse only when ready, follow the institution instructions and retain the original securely until the deposit is finally credited under bank guidance. Do not redeposit the same check.

Split deposit can automate saving, but leave enough in checking for bills and a buffer. Start with an amount that survives a low-pay period. An automatic savings transfer that repeatedly causes overdrafts is not successful saving.

Check the first two deposits manually. Confirm routing, amount, timing and account ownership. If an employer changes payroll provider or asks for new bank details through an unexpected message, verify the request independently.
The account step passes when pay arrives without avoidable fees, the worker can access it safely, and one compromised card or forgotten password does not put every dollar at risk.

sections.heading: Set the Four Amounts from Real Cash Flow
paragraphs: The four jobs are a sequence, not a universal percentage formula. Someone living independently with rent due may need almost all of a partial first check for operations. Someone with family support may be able to seed the buffer, clear a costly balance and start retirement immediately. Both can use the same order honestly.

Start with a payday worksheet containing net pay at the top and the next expected deposit date beside it. Subtract only costs due before that date. Monthly budgets can conceal timing: a bill due tomorrow has a different claim on cash than one due after another paycheck.

Give irregular income a base and an upside rule. Build essentials from a conservative number such as scheduled hours, not the best possible commission or overtime. When extra income actually clears, divide it with a preset rule across buffer, priority obligation, future goal and enjoyment.

For an illustrative $750 net check, a worker might reserve $500 for operations, move $75 to a buffer, pay $100 extra toward a card and put $75 toward a matched retirement contribution or goal. Those figures are examples, not recommendations. Actual due dates and risks control.

Percentages become more useful after two or three complete pay cycles establish normal net income. Until then, choose dollar amounts that protect the period ahead. A 20 percent savings target that causes a $35 overdraft fee has failed its cash-flow purpose.

Use separate ledger lines even if all money remains in one account. Account separation can help, but labels are what prevent double counting. “Bills: $420,” “buffer: $75” and “spendable: $55” are clearer than a $550 account balance.

Couples and households should distinguish personal income from shared obligations. Decide whether contributions are fixed, proportional to net income or assigned by bill. The first paycheck should not silently establish a household arrangement nobody discussed.

If income is extremely tight, the future job may initially be benefit enrollment or gathering plan information rather than a large cash contribution. The constraint job may be a negotiated hardship call rather than an extra payment. Each job can begin with an action as well as dollars.

Review the allocation before buying, not after the balance falls. Banking alerts at a chosen threshold can reinforce the plan, but alerts do not replace a ledger because pending card transactions and scheduled debits may not appear in available balance consistently.

The four amounts are correct when they protect the next pay period, reduce fragility and can be repeated. They do not need to impress anyone, match an online template or use every last dollar. A small unassigned checking cushion can prevent ordinary timing from becoming a fee.

Build a low-pay version of the plan before it is needed. State which optional transfer pauses first, which bills remain protected and whom to contact if hours are cut. This avoids deciding under pressure and keeps a temporary income drop from triggering several fees at once.

Also build a high-pay rule. For example, after required costs and taxes are checked, extra net pay can be divided among the buffer, priority debt, future goal and a defined reward. A preset rule lets the worker enjoy progress without turning an unusually strong check into a permanently higher lifestyle. Revisit both rules promptly after a raise, move or benefit change.

sections.heading: Job One: Carry the Worker to the Next Payday
paragraphs: The first allocation funds essential life and continued employment. List housing contribution, food, transport, phone, childcare, medication, insurance and debt minimums due before the next reliable income. Use dates and amounts, not a monthly category total.

Calculate daily flexible money only after fixed obligations are reserved. If $280 remains for fourteen days, that is a $20 average across food, transport and personal needs—not an invitation to spend $280 on day one.

Place due money in a bills subaccount or clearly labeled ledger category. Separation is useful only when the account has no fee or minimum that defeats the purpose. The goal is to prevent available balance from masquerading as spendable balance.

Budget work costs first. Transit passes, fuel, non-slip shoes, uniforms, certification, tools, meals and data can be necessary to earn the next check. Verify which costs the employer must provide or reimburse before paying personally.

Plan one modest celebration with a fixed amount. A first paycheck deserves recognition, and a deliberate reward makes the system more sustainable. The amount should not require credit or delay an essential bill.

Do not begin financing a car, phone or furniture because annual salary sounds large. Convert all ownership costs—payment, insurance, tax, maintenance, fuel and repair—into the same pay-cycle budget and test them against several normal checks.

When living with family, agree on a contribution that names what it covers and when it begins. Avoid an informal amount that expands whenever the account balance is visible. Recurring support belongs in the cash-flow plan.
Use a 24-hour pause for nonessential purchases above a chosen threshold during the first month. The pause protects against the temporary feeling that every future check is already guaranteed.

If the first check cannot cover essentials, prioritize immediate consequences and contact providers early. Seek local benefits, worker, housing or debt guidance where appropriate. Avoid payday loans or paycheck advances until the full cost and alternatives are understood.
Job one is complete when required costs through the next payday are reserved and the worker can keep showing up. Everything else is allocated from the true remainder.

sections.heading: Job Two: Build a Buffer Before Chasing Returns
paragraphs: A starter buffer prevents a small expense from becoming expensive debt. Its first target can be the largest likely short-term disruption: transport repair, a medical copay, a missed shift or a required work item. Choose an amount based on actual exposure.

Keep the starter reserve liquid and separate from daily spending. An insured savings account can work; volatile investments, retirement accounts and locked products are poor tools for a bill that may arrive next week.

[[S3|FDIC guidance for young adults]] recommends an insured account, direct deposit and a budget that tracks earnings, goals and expenses. The point is control and safety, not finding the highest possible return on a tiny emergency balance.

Automate a fixed dollar or percentage each payday after checking cash flow. A fixed dollar is predictable; a percentage adapts to variable hours. Either method should pause before creating an overdraft or missed bill.

Name the reserve and its use rules. “Work and emergency buffer” is clearer than “savings.” Define eligible uses and a refill plan. Planned entertainment and annual gifts need separate sinking funds so the emergency account is not repeatedly raided.
Build in stages: one paycheck of core expenses, then a month, then a household-specific longer target. Job stability, health, dependents and housing obligations matter more than a universal number.
The late savings photograph will show cash beside a laptop and piggy bank because the buffer is a bridge between income and disruption. Cash itself is not the goal; continuity is.
Do not wait for a perfect budget. Even a small automatic amount creates evidence that saving happens on payday rather than only if money remains. Increase it after normal pay and expenses are known.

Keep the account accessible but not frictionless. Removing the debit card from a mobile wallet or using a separate savings account can slow impulse transfers without making emergency access impossible.
Job two is complete for the first paycheck when a deliberate amount reaches the reserve and the rules are written. The target can grow over many checks; the habit starts now.

sections.heading: Job Three: Remove the Most Expensive Constraint
paragraphs: After essentials and a starter buffer, direct money toward the obligation causing the greatest harm. That may be past-due rent, a utility shutoff, high-rate credit, a tax deadline, a required work expense or money borrowed from family under a clear agreement.

List every debt with borrower, balance, annual rate, minimum, due date, fees, collateral and delinquency. A small balance is not automatically the priority if another account can cause eviction, repossession or a much higher cost.

Keep minimum payments current while choosing one extra-payment target, unless a qualified hardship plan says otherwise. Automate minimums only when the checking balance and pay timing can support them.

Credit-card interest can erase the satisfaction of a one-time purchase long after the first paycheck. Paying a statement balance by the due date can avoid interest on purchases when the account retains a grace period, but contract terms control.

Avoid treating “buy now, pay later” as a budgeting category. Multiple small installments can stack across pay periods and obscure the remaining cash. Record every scheduled debit beside ordinary bills.

If family funded education, transport or relocation, agree whether repayment is a gift, flexible support or contractual obligation. Put recurring repayment in the plan without surrendering control of the whole paycheck.

Before refinancing or consolidating, compare total interest, fees, term, variable rates, lost protections and collateral. A lower monthly payment can cost more overall and keep the first-job budget constrained longer.

Use windfalls carefully. Overtime, bonus or reimbursement should not fund recurring lifestyle costs. Apply a prewritten percentage to the priority debt, buffer and one goal after taxes and near-term bills are checked.

Check the employer for legitimate student-loan, transport, education or emergency-assistance benefits. Understand eligibility and tax treatment. Do not pay a third party an upfront fee to “unlock” an employer or government benefit.

Job three is complete when the first extra dollar has one verified target and the payment does not recreate the debt elsewhere. Progress is a system, not a dramatic zero balance followed by an empty checking account.

sections.heading: Job Four: Buy Future Options Through Benefits and Goals
paragraphs: The future job begins with employer benefits whose enrollment window may close. Review health coverage, retirement plan, match, disability, life insurance, paid leave, education, commuter support and flexible accounts. Missing a deadline can matter more than squeezing another percentage point from a savings account.

For retirement, read eligibility, automatic enrollment, contribution type, employer match, vesting, fees and investment default. [[S4|The Department of Labor notes]] that workers are always vested in their own 401(k) contributions, while employer contributions can follow a vesting schedule depending on the plan.

Capture an employer match when affordable after essential cash needs, because it can add employer money tied to the worker’s contribution. Translate the match formula into dollars and check whether each payday matters. Do not contribute so aggressively that rent returns to a credit card.

Health-plan enrollment should compare premium, deductible, network, prescriptions and maximum covered exposure. Remaining on a parent’s plan, where lawful, does not automatically make employer coverage unnecessary; compare coordination, cost and HSA implications.

Disability coverage can protect the income stream that every goal depends on. Review benefit percentage, cap, waiting period, definition, tax treatment and portability. First-job workers often have little savings to bridge a long absence.

Choose one visible medium-term goal—a credential, reliable vehicle, move, education, travel or equipment—and calculate amount, date and payday contribution. A concrete goal competes better with lifestyle inflation than “save more.”

Do not invest money needed within a short, fixed period in assets whose value can fall before the deadline. Match account risk and access to the goal. Keep emergency and bill money out of speculative products.

Verify beneficiary designations for retirement and life coverage. A beneficiary form can control separately from a will. Update after major relationship changes and avoid naming someone merely because onboarding feels rushed.
Increase future funding when pay rises. Precommit part of each raise before lifestyle absorbs it. The first-check percentage can be small while the rule for future increases is strong.
Job four is complete when enrollment deadlines are met, valuable employer money is understood and one future goal receives an automatic or scheduled contribution.

sections.heading: Check Withholding Before the Refund Becomes the Plan
paragraphs: Income-tax withholding is a prepayment toward expected tax, not a savings account and not the final tax calculation. A large refund can mean too much was withheld; a balance due can mean too little, though credits and circumstances matter.

The midpoint photograph shows an income-tax note, calculator and pen because the first pay statement supplies evidence for a withholding check. One small partial-period check can be misleading; use the estimator again after a normal check or major income change.

[[S5|IRS Publication 505]] explains that Form W-4 information, wages and household circumstances determine withholding. The IRS Tax Withholding Estimator can help many employees decide whether to submit a revised W-4.

Check carefully when the worker has multiple jobs, a working spouse, self-employment income, significant investment income, dependents, credits or a part-year job. Each employer sees only information provided for that job.

Do not claim exemption from withholding because income feels low without meeting the official requirements. Exemption from federal income-tax withholding does not necessarily remove payroll taxes, state obligations or the duty to file.

Keep privacy in mind. The IRS guidance provides ways to adjust additional withholding without necessarily describing all outside income to an employer. Use official instructions or qualified tax help for a complex household.

State and local withholding can use separate forms and rules. Confirm work location and residence treatment, especially for remote or cross-border work. Federal changes do not automatically correct state withholding.

Save the submitted W-4 confirmation and inspect a later pay statement. Payroll implementation can lag. Compare year-to-date withholding with the estimator again after raises, bonuses, marriage, a second job or dependent changes.

A tax refund should not be the only emergency plan. If withholding is intentionally conservative, understand the cash-flow cost. If adjusted downward, automate part of the larger net check to the goal so it does not disappear into spending.
The withholding step passes when the worker understands why tax lines appear, has checked material complexity and schedules a recheck. Precision improves with evidence across the year.

sections.heading: Protect the Paycheck from Lifestyle Creep and Fraud
paragraphs: New income attracts recurring costs quickly: premium phone plans, subscriptions, food delivery, a financed vehicle and expectations from others. A recurring $40 decision is not just $40; it claims part of every future paycheck until canceled.

Wait through two or three normal pay cycles before raising fixed living costs. Track the true net average and work expenses. Overtime, training pay and bonuses should not be used as the base for permanent obligations.

Create a personal spending amount that can be used without guilt after the four jobs are funded. Extreme restriction often rebounds; undefined freedom often expands. A fixed amount makes both trade-offs visible.

Never pay someone to release wages, buy gift cards for payroll verification, move money through a personal account or return part of an employer check. Verify unexpected instructions using a known employer contact.

Fake-check scams can show funds as available before the bank discovers the check is fraudulent. Do not send money onward because a new employer, client or equipment vendor overpaid. Legitimate payroll does not require an employee to redistribute a check.

Protect the pay statement and onboarding records. Criminals can use payroll portals and direct-deposit changes to redirect wages. Use multifactor authentication, alerts and a separate verification step for bank-detail changes.

Be cautious with early-wage-access and cash-advance products. Compare tips, subscriptions, expedited fees and repeat use with the amount advanced. Accessing earned wages early can leave the next payday unable to cover its own bills.

If helping family, choose an amount or percentage after core costs and reserve. Avoid sharing the live account balance as an invitation to negotiate every purchase. Sustainable support protects both parties longer.

Review subscriptions and recurring card charges on the second and fourth paychecks. Cancel what is not used and save confirmation. Trials begun as a first-paycheck reward can become silent annual costs.
The protection step passes when fixed costs wait for stable evidence, fraud controls are active and generosity or celebration remains inside a deliberate amount.

sections.heading: Run a 30-Day Paycheck Operating Plan
paragraphs: On payday one, reconcile the statement, reserve bills through the next payday, move the starter buffer, make the priority payment and fund one future goal. Record every transfer so movement between accounts is not mistaken for spending.

Within forty-eight hours, complete urgent benefit enrollment, verify direct deposit and activate account alerts. Put payroll, enrollment and tax contacts in a secure note. Do not store passwords there.

At the end of week one, compare planned with actual transport, food and work costs. Adjust the next-week amount rather than declaring the budget failed. First-job estimates improve only when observed.
Before payday two, check pending bills and account balance. Verify that split deposits and automatic transfers did not cause a shortage. Change amounts before the next payroll cutoff if necessary.
On payday two, repeat the same four jobs using the new evidence. Keep the sequence stable even if percentages change. A routine reduces the number of decisions made while excited or tired.

At day thirty, calculate average net pay, essential cost per pay period, buffer progress, debt change, benefit deductions and goal contribution. Do not annualize irregular overtime without a conservative base case.

Write one improvement for the next ninety days: raise the buffer transfer, capture the full match, remove one fee, finish a small debt or fund a credential. One controlled change is more likely to survive than a total financial makeover.
Keep pay records and update contact or withholding information through verified employer systems. Reconcile the W-2 when it arrives after year-end. Report discrepancies promptly.

The first-paycheck photograph sequence ends with cash beside a laptop and savings container because the milestone becomes valuable when money is converted into continuity and options, not displayed as a temporary balance.
The operating plan succeeds when the next paycheck arrives to a system already prepared for it. Each future check can then improve the proportions without reinventing the order.

summary: Treat the first paycheck as a systems test. Verify the pay period, rate, hours, earnings, deductions and deposit before spending. A first check may cover a partial period or omit benefits that begin later, so do not build permanent costs from one amount.

Use net pay rather than salary headlines. Give the check four jobs: carry essential life and work costs to the next payday, build a starter buffer, reduce the most expensive constraint and fund benefits or a future goal.

Read every pay-statement line. Match regular and overtime hours, rate, commission, reimbursements, taxes and voluntary deductions with time records and onboarding elections. Save statements securely and report errors promptly in writing.

Choose a safe, low-fee place for wages. Compare insured bank or credit-union accounts, payroll cards and checks by fees, access, protections and timing. Employers offering payroll cards must provide another payment option under applicable federal rules.

Reserve housing, food, transport, phone, childcare, medication, insurance and debt minimums due before the next reliable income. Include work costs and one fixed celebration amount. Do not finance a permanent upgrade from a partial first check.

Build a liquid starter buffer for the disruption most likely to threaten work or bills. Automate a sustainable dollar or percentage, give the reserve clear use rules and grow it in stages instead of waiting for a perfect target.

List debts by balance, rate, minimum, due date, collateral and delinquency. Keep required minimums current and send extra money to one verified priority without emptying checking and recreating the debt elsewhere.

Review benefit deadlines immediately. Understand health coverage, retirement eligibility and match, vesting, disability, leave and education support. Capture valuable employer money only at a contribution level that leaves essentials financeable.

Use official IRS tools to check withholding after a normal pay cycle and after material changes. Multiple jobs, self-employment, dependents, marriage, part-year work and state rules can make one employer’s default withholding inaccurate.

Wait through several normal pay cycles before increasing fixed lifestyle costs. Put part of future raises toward savings or debt before the entire increase becomes recurring spending. Keep a deliberate personal-spending amount to avoid all-or-nothing behavior.

Protect payroll credentials and bank changes with multifactor authentication and independent verification. Never pay to unlock wages, return an overpayment, buy gift cards for an employer or route company money through a personal account.

At thirty days, calculate average net pay, essential cost, buffer, debt progress, benefit deductions and goal funding. Choose one improvement for the next ninety days. The first paycheck matters most when it creates a process every later paycheck can repeat.

Do not force a universal percentage formula onto a partial or variable check. Put the next deposit date beside net pay, reserve only costs due before then and use conservative scheduled income as the base. Divide overtime or commission only after it clears.

Keep allocation categories visible even if the money stays in one account. A labeled ledger prevents the full balance from appearing spendable and exposes pending bills. Household contributions should be discussed as fixed, proportional or bill-specific rather than established silently.

Match the account to the time horizon. Bills and emergency reserves need stability and access; a fixed near-term goal should not depend on volatile investments. Retirement and other long-horizon goals can use the employer plan or appropriate investment options after fees and risk are understood.

Protect the ability to keep earning. Transport, work clothing, tools, childcare and connectivity can rank ahead of optional debt prepayment because they make the next check possible. Verify reimbursement rules before paying an employer expense personally. Keep receipts and written approval until the reimbursement fully clears.

faq.question: Why is a first paycheck smaller than expected?
faq.answer: It may cover a partial pay period and include taxes, benefits or other authorized deductions from gross earnings.

faq.question: What should be funded first?
faq.answer: Reserve essential living and work costs through the next payday before optional purchases or aggressive investing.

faq.question: Is direct deposit always free?
faq.answer: The deposit itself often has no fee, but the receiving account can still charge maintenance, ATM or overdraft fees.

faq.question: Should a first paycheck go into retirement?
faq.answer: Review eligibility and any match promptly, then contribute only at a level that preserves essential cash flow.

faq.question: How much should go to emergency savings?
faq.answer: Start with a sustainable amount tied to likely short-term disruption and build the reserve over successive checks.

faq.question: When should withholding be checked?
faq.answer: After a normal pay statement and whenever jobs, income, dependents, marital status or outside income change materially.

glossary.definition: Earnings before taxes and other deductions are subtracted.
The amount remaining after payroll deductions, often called take-home pay.
The dates during which the earnings on a paycheck were generated.
A cumulative payroll total from the start of the calendar year through the current statement.
Tax money an employer sends to a taxing authority based on wages and employee information.
Electronic delivery of wages to an account selected under the payroll arrangement.
The point at which a worker has a nonforfeitable right to specified employer contributions.
Cash kept available to absorb timing differences and small unexpected costs.
